=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/opencode_helpers.sh:121-135 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When the provider probe reports `down`, the helper suppresses the per-call alert without ensuring an outage tracker or tracker alert exists.
  WHY: Fail-open callers may let the job succeed, skipping the failure-only tracker path and leaving the outage untracked and unalerted; severity disagreement: one reviewer rated this NIT, while another rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:244-260 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The cached probe result has no age limit, so a cached `down` or `unknown` result can suppress later alerts for the rest of the job.
  WHY: A transient probe failure can remain cached after recovery and cause alerts for unrelated runtime failures to be suppressed; severity disagreement: one reviewer rated this MAJOR, while others rated it NIT.
- scripts/opencode_helpers.sh:129 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The probe cache passed to `cached_probe` has no age limit.
  WHY: A cached `down` or `unknown` result can suppress later alerts even after the provider recovers.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:596-609 | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_write_output` and `_write_alert` swallow `OSError` without logging the failure.
  WHY: Filesystem write failures can leave tracking state stale or drop operator alerts without diagnosis.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:671 | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `OUTAGE_RUN_ID` may be empty if `run_refs[0].run_id` is absent.
  WHY: Subsequent logic may rely on a valid run ID or workflow name.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3349 | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The "Record Claude pool capacity" step sources a staged script.
  WHY: Sourcing an untrusted or staged script is a trust boundary, even though the implementation is consistent with other bootstrap steps.
- tests/test_opencode_helpers.py:256 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_alert_with_probe` creates a temporary directory that is never removed.
  WHY: Test runs accumulate temporary directories on the runner.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: “If the codex/OpenCode fallback succeeds,” treat the capacity event as recovered and send a “recovered” alert after the deduplicated capacity alert.
  expected_change_site: `scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_pool_capacity.sh` and the Claude-to-Codex/OpenCode fallback success path
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: `scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_pool_capacity.sh` opens the capacity tracker for `all_gated` and closes it only when the pool reports an available account; `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` has no fallback-success path to close the tracker or send the recovery alert; `scripts/ai_engine.sh` suppresses its own alert after the capacity alert but does not close the tracker or send a recovered alert.
- requirement: Re-run only stable release runs that “failed only on `provider_unavailable`”.
  expected_change_site: `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh` release-run classification and `scripts/provider_outage.py` release resume
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: The intake records a release run when provider-error evidence exists and the live probe is down, without verifying that unrelated failures were absent; when reruns are enabled, the resume path reruns each recorded run.
- requirement: "While it is open, the review sweep (review_autofix_sweep.yml) probes before enumerating: down or inconclusive skips review dispatches" and "Consumers get the same pass from the `provider-outage-resume` job of `ai-review.yml`."
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/ai-review.yml
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The consumer job gates on `schedule` and its pause output is only written when the sweep subcommand runs; there is no subsequent dispatch step that reads `paused` or an equivalent guard on the consumer dispatch path.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- `scripts/opencode_helpers.sh` lines 121-135, the `case "${failure_class}"` block in `opencode_emit_failure_alert` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the probe reports `down`, the per-call ERROR alert is suppressed and the function returns. Nothing there opens the `ai:provider-outage` tracker.
  WHY: Some callers fail open and do not fail the job, so the failure-path steps that open the tracker do not run.
- `scripts/provider_outage.py` `cached_probe`, lines 246-260, used with `RUNTIME_DIR/provider_outage_alert_probe.json` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The cached probe result has no age limit, and `down` and `unknown` results are cached as well as `up`.
  WHY: A brief probe failure can cache `down` for the rest of a job, suppressing alerts even after the provider recovers.
- `tests/test_opencode_helpers.py` `_alert_with_probe`, `tempfile.mkdtemp()` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The temporary directory is never removed.
  WHY: Each call leaves a temporary directory behind on the CI runner.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: Q3 (AD-3) says the capacity event gets "one deduplicated capacity alert plus a 'recovered' alert", and the tracker closes once the codex/OpenCode fallback succeeds.
  Expected change site: `scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_pool_capacity.sh` and the `Record Claude pool capacity` step in `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`.
  Evidence of absence: The `all_gated` branch opens the `kind=capacity` tracker. The tracker closes only when `steps.claude_pool.outputs.available == 'true'` on a later run. Nothing closes it, or sends the recovery alert, when the fallback itself succeeds.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: Re-run only a stable release run that "failed only on `provider_unavailable`".
  Expected change site: `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh` (release-run recording) and `scripts/provider_outage.py` (`resume` release-run block).
  Evidence of absence: The intake records a release run when its logs contain provider-error evidence and the live probe is down. It does not check that the run had no other failures. With `PROVIDER_OUTAGE_RELEASE_RERUN_ENABLED=true`, `resume` calls `rerun-failed-jobs` for every recorded run.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/opencode_helpers.sh:121-135 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the provider probe reports `down`, the helper suppresses the per-call alert without ensuring that a tracker is opened.
  WHY: If the caller succeeds after the probe is checked, the workflow failure path that records the outage never runs, leaving it neither tracked nor alerted.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:605 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_write_output` and `_write_alert` swallow `OSError` without logging the failure.
  WHY: Filesystem write failures during the sweep or probe can leave stale tracking state or cause missed operator alerts.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:671 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `OUTAGE_RUN_ID` may be empty if `run_refs[0].run_id` is absent.
  WHY: The fallback produces an empty string, and subsequent logic may rely on it being a valid ID or workflow name.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3349 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The "Record Claude pool capacity" step sources a staged script.
  WHY: Sourcing an untrusted or staged script is a trust boundary, even though the implementation is consistent with other bootstrap steps.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: If the codex/OpenCode fallback succeeds, the run should be treated as recovered, with “one deduplicated capacity alert plus a ‘recovered’ alert.”
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml, “Record Claude pool capacity” and the fallback completion path.
  Evidence of absence: `scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_pool_capacity.sh` opens the capacity tracker and sends its alert when the Claude pool reports `all_gated`, but there is no corresponding fallback-success path in the workflow or the scripts that closes the tracker or sends the recovery alert.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: Re-run only stable release runs that “failed only on the provider outage.”
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh release-run classification and scripts/provider_outage.py release resume.
  Evidence of absence: The heal intake records a release run when its logs contain provider-error evidence and the live probe is down. It does not verify that the run's other failures were absent.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/opencode_helpers.sh lines 121-135 (the new case branch that invokes provider_outage.py probe and the cached_probe at scripts/provider_outage.py:244-260) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The suppression decision reads a cached result with no age check, so an early `down` result can suppress later runtime failure alerts after provider recovery.
  WHY: A later unrelated runtime failure can have its alert suppressed even when the provider is healthy.
- scripts/opencode_helpers.sh lines 121-135 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The suppression returns the original `${alert_rc}` without creating or touching the `ai:provider-outage` tracker.
  WHY: Fail-open callers can suppress an outage alert and succeed, so neither the tracker nor an alert is produced.
- scripts/provider_outage.py lines 596-609 (`_write_output` and `_write_alert`) | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Both helpers swallow `OSError` and return without logging.
  WHY: Filesystem write failures can silently leave the sweep output stale or drop an alert.
- tests/test_opencode_helpers.py line 256 in `_alert_with_probe` | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `tempfile.mkdtemp()` creates a directory that is never removed.
  WHY: Test-only temporary directories accumulate over repeated test runs.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "While it is open, the review sweep (review_autofix_sweep.yml) probes before enumerating: down or inconclusive skips review dispatches" and "Consumers get the same pass from the `provider-outage-resume` job of `ai-review.yml`."

  Evidence of absence: The new job's `if:` is `github.event_name == 'schedule' && vars.PROVIDER_OUTAGE_RESUME_ENABLED != 'false'`. The "schedule" gate is the trigger. The pause path through the sweep step uses `steps.provider_outage.outputs.paused`, but `paused` is only written when the sweep subcommand runs. Either the consumer job should be renamed and call sweep + dispatch in the same way the source sweep does, or the agents.md description and the changelog fragment need to be amended to make the consumer pause semantics clear.
